llm.summary: The skill's instructions generally match its stated purpose (controlling a local BLE vibrator via a local HTTP bridge) but it asks the user to fetch and run an external repository (the URL is a placeholder) and the registry metadata doesn't reflect the macOS-only limitation — those gaps are concerning and deserve caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description match the actions described (calling a local HTTP server that broadcasts BLE commands). However the skill is macOS-only per SKILL.md but the registry metadata lists no OS restriction; the skill also references an external repo (YOUR_REPO_URL) that is not provided. Those omissions reduce provenance and clarity.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to running a local bridge server, sniffing to obtain a local device pairing ID, editing a local Python file, and making local HTTP POST/GET calls via curl. The agent is only instructed to call local endpoints; the instructions do not ask the agent to read unrelated system files or exfiltrate data. Still, they tell a human to run arbitrary code from an external repo, which expands the operational surface.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no embedded code or install spec in the skill; instead the README instructs the user to git clone an external repository (placeholder YOUR_REPO_URL) and run its code. Fetching and running an external repo is high-risk unless the repo URL and provenance are known and trusted. The absence of a concrete, vetted download source is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths and the instructions do not request unrelated secrets. The only local data required is the device pairing ID (captured by the sniff step), which is reasonable for this hardware integration.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills or agent-wide settings. It instructs running a local server on port 8888, which is normal for a bridge service and limited in scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to describe exactly how to control a local Venus/Cachito toy, but it relies on running code from an external repository that is not provided in the SKILL.md. Before installing or following instructions: 1) Obtain and inspect the actual repository source (do not run code from an unknown URL). 2) Verify the repo owner and review the server.py and sniff_cachito.py code for any unexpected network calls, logging, or sensitive-data exfiltration. 3) Note the SKILL.md is macOS-only — do not attempt to run the bridge on other OSes. 4) If you plan to run the bridge inside Docker or on a multi-user machine, consider firewalling the local port (8888) or using local-only binding to prevent other hosts from reaching the service. If you cannot verify the repository or you are uncomfortable running third-party binaries/scripts, do not install or run the bridge.
